Lena — thanks for the sample and the sizing. Quick technical outline and recommended path forward from the serving team:

Plan summary:
- Phased backfill: category by category (high‑traffic categories first) over 48–72 hours. Each category window is a rolling ingestion + index verify step.
- Vector store choice: we recommend starting with our managed vectorstore (Redwood Hosted VectorStore) using 8‑bit PQ quantization for cost savings, with the option to pin to a float16 instance if you need micro‑precision for exact matches.
- Batching and KV caching: we’ll enable continuous batching on generation traffic and warm KV caches for top 50k tokens to avoid cold latency spikes.

Rerank evals & acceptance criteria (draft):
- Baseline metrics: MRR and top‑1 relevance on a 500‑query evaluation set (we will co‑create queries with Stellar).
- Regression tolerance: <2% relative drop in MRR vs current production ranker during canary window.
- Latency SLOs: P95 end‑to‑end for the rerank call <= 120ms for top‑10 candidate rerank.
- Automated smoke checks: token cost per 1k queries, embedding ingestion error rate <0.5%, and vector NN recall > 98% after each category backfill.

Risks & mitigations:
- Large initial cold index: mitigate by staging a seeded index with high‑traffic categories first and running a synthetic traffic replay.
- Vectorstore mismatch across versions: we’ll pin model versions and add an automated fallback to the text‑only ranker if similarity search fails.

I’ve uploaded a detailed execution workbook (index_backfill_plan.xlsx) and a draft rerank acceptance doc (rerank_eval_criteria.pdf) to the shared Drive. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcDeFGhIJkL_migration-plan

Next steps I can take tomorrow:
- Kick off a staging ingestion job and share the staging cluster endpoint.
- Prepare a short canary runbook with rollback thresholds.

–Marcus

Subject: Re: Kickoff: embedding backfill & rerank cutover — initial asks

Folks —

Some implementation notes from the infra/engineering side:
- Ingestion pipelines: we’ll use incremental ingestion jobs built on top of your CSV export. Each job produces a Parquet payload and a tokenized text blob for embedding. Jobs are idempotent (upserts by SKU id).
- Vector shard sizing: for ~4.2M items with 1536‑dim embeddings, target 128 shards (we’ll evaluate based on observed throughput).
- Staging checklist (engineer tasks):
  * Create staging index (tagged v0.1)
  * Run warmup replay 12h before canary
  * Execute smoke queries and generate embedding drift report
  * Run automated rerank A/B test on 5k test queries

Open questions:
- Do you have any PII in metadata fields we should mask? (Lena — mentioned variants but not PII)
- For rollback, preferred mechanism: full index swap vs per‑shard fallback? We recommend index swap for simplicity.

I’ll raise PRs for the ingestion configs later today.

—Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Software Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Thanks — that plan looks reasonable. A couple clarifications from our side:
- Canary size: suggest starting with 2% of traffic (route via header flag) for 24 hours, then 10% for 6 hours before 100% if metrics look good.
- Rollback threshold: if top‑1 relevance drops >1.5% absolute or latency >150ms p95, rollback immediately.

Also — can you add a short section in the runbook about how we validate the vectorstore quantization (spot checks to ensure similar neighbors are preserved after PQ). We want to avoid any surprises from 8‑bit approximations.

Tom Wu
Platform Lead, Acme Search (partner consultancy)
tom.wu@acme-search.com
